versions.name: RXV2-0.9.889-save-bar
versions.notes: The floating Save bar comes back after typing in a box: it hides only while a box is being typed in and the keyboard covers the window, measured zoom-proof (height x scale). A page zoomed in - by a pinch, or by iOS itself on focusing a small box - read as 'covered' before, and the bar stayed hidden for good (Malcolm, the Travel page). The leftover 2026-08-06 ride-up code that re-lifted the bar on every scroll is removed.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.888-hobbywing-v4
versions.notes: The ESC settings page answers for the brand the flight controller is set to (a Hobbywing V4 owner was told to 'set it to Scorpion'): the Scorpion is read and changed there; a Hobbywing Platinum V4 is read-only for Rotorflight (LCD box / WiFi module); the Platinum V5, FlyRotor, OpenYGE and XDFly are programmable but not from that page yet. Wiring + help: the Platinum V4's telemetry is its programming port's signal pin, never the red pin.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.887-direct-drive
versions.notes: The gear-ratio page accepts 1 : 1 as direct drive (head speed = motor RPM) with an amber note that it is also the factory setting; it called 1 : 1 'Not set' and asked to save anyway. Found on the SAB Havoc.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.886-arm-live
versions.notes: The phone's Switches page keeps its live line while the model is armed: the receiver answers that one read (MSP_RC) from its own output without a word to the flight controller, the ARMED banner is a strip on that page, and an arm switch written from a page moves the arming channel the receiver watches at once (it was learned once at boot and never again).

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.885-failsafe-ticks
versions.notes: The receiver honours the transmitter's failsafe ticks: only the ticked channels move on signal loss, the rest hold (older firmware moved all 16). Rescue page: climb time 0 means no climb, it levels and hovers. Governor page: idle and auto throttle shown and typed in per cent, and the bail-out help put right.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.884-cli-prompt-not-a-comment
versions.notes: The command line's reply was taken as ended at any "# " that a USB packet happened to end on - a diff is full of comment lines that begin so, which is why a long diff all ended at the same 347 lines every time. The prompt is now "# " at a line's start followed by silence.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.883-cli-long-replies
versions.notes: A command line reply the flight controller is still printing after the wait (a diff all of every bank) now comes back as its start with 202, and /api/cli/out gives the rest until it is whole; before, what had come in six seconds went out as the whole reply. The phone's command line page fetches the rest too.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.882-cli-diff-all-whole
versions.notes: The command line keeps a whole diff all (up to 64 kB; it kept only the last 16,000 characters, so the head of a long diff was lost, on the phone's command line and the transmitter's Diff to card).

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.881-cli-from-the-transmitter
versions.notes: The command line (USB cable) may be used from a linked transmitter when the safety is on: the transmitter's new Command line page and Diff to card use it. A linked transmitter with the arming channel high, or none set, is refused as before.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.880-adjustment-lines-known
versions.notes: The receiver keeps a copy of the flight controller's adjustment lines as they pass through it (every read over the USB cable, every write from the app or the transmitter) and serves it to the app, so the Switches page now shows the bank selector as the flight controller really has it - the travel the transmitter set, in the slot it lives in - and a Save there writes that slot and removes any duplicate line instead of adding one.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.879-switch-one-line
versions.notes: A switch on the Adjustments page is one Rotorflight line, so it works at every change (one line per position worked once per power-up: Rotorflight applies a fixed value only the first time); switches found in the old form are converted when the page opens: save to keep them. After a transmitter-on boot the receiver takes one look (a scan) for the home WiFi when the transmitter goes off or the model is disarmed, and joins if it is there.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.878-fresh-block-reads
versions.notes: A transmitter asking for a block of settings (PIDs, rates, governor) now gets a fresh read, never the cached values from before its bank switch moved: the Version 2 transmitter could keep showing the previous bank's PIDs.

rotorflight.line: Rotorflight 2.3 — the release these pages are written and tested against.
